note:
v1 96.751/96.765. PERIOD DOUBLING, polytempo braindance in Bohlen-Pierce tuning (13 steps to the 3:1 tritave, Lambda mode; no octaves anywhere): a clock that learns to drift.
- One number drives everything: the logistic map x <- r x (1-x), iterated each sixteenth, plays the lead on chirp's physical reed (clarinet: odd harmonics, BP's natural voice). It also decides the drum accents, ratchets and stutter chance.
- r walks the road into chaos section by section: one note (a sequencer pulse, after a damped wobble), two (7/8), four (with a rest), eight (5/4), chaos (the tempo ramping 140 -> 150), the PERIOD-THREE window (r 3.835: three sixteenths running across the 4/4), the storm (r 4, 11/8 at 154), then settling back to one note as it slows to 132.
- Polytempo: blips on a 5:4 grid from the map's twin, a folded-sine bass on a 3:4 grid. BP 3:5:7 chords on a glass pad. Meter changes and tempo ramps live in the tempo map.
Spectrum: v1 at first was 10-19 dB heavy at 70-640 Hz and 10-17 dB dull above 4 kHz (folded bass, 909 body); the bass came down 9 dB, the kick 4 dB with an hp, and a ride and louder hats came in: spectrum 20 -> 92, cohesion 12 -> 100. Flow 46: t8's tail differs (+28 dB at 300-600 Hz on my side); a ticking intro to meet it cost variety, so it was dropped. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
next: The in-seam with t8; a voice? (t6 holds voice); warp the lead in the chaos?

note:
v2 96.594/96.605 (v1 rescored on 8ef47431 96.768/96.809; kept on judgment: a big systems-and-tuning pass, -0.2). THE CLOCK DRIFTS OUT OF TUNE AND BACK (T9_R2=drift), on wM's tunings, systems and morph.
- The song's tuning is 12-TET while the map holds one and two notes: the Bohlen-Pierce lines snap to semitones, a plain sequencer. It ramps into exact Bohlen-Pierce across the period-four section, stays alien through eight, chaos, the window and the storm, and ramps back to 12-TET as it settles. The tuning bifurcates with the map.
- In the chaos and the storm a second glass pad plays the 3:5:7 chords CROSS-SYNTHESISED with the drum bus (morph mode cross keyed by drums), so the chords breathe in the chaotic rhythm.
- A second logistic map at r 3.95, as a song var, throws the reed around the stereo field.
- The tuning's A3 root also puts the bass and bell on the lead's Bohlen-Pierce lattice; in v1 the A1 bass sat on its own.
Flow 48 -> 43: the head is now 12-TET against t8's tail. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: The seam with t8 (43); a voice in the window?

note:
v3 96.824/96.842 (v2 rescored on b4151423 96.782/96.815). IT COMES BACK IN THREES (T9_R3=sing), on wM's singing voice.
- In the period-three window a human voice SINGS "it comes back in threes" (chirp tts --sing "A3/8 C4 E4" --repeat 3, humanize 0.4), twice. Five syllables on a three-note tune, so the words land on different notes each time round, while the logistic map cycles in threes under them.
- Its notes snap to the song's Bohlen-Pierce tuning there. It returns once, softer, as the map settles, by then back in 12-TET: the same words in a different tuning.

PALETTE round. v4 96.918/96.941 (v3 rescored now 96.709/96.731). T9_R4=break.
- KIT: machine-kit (on 9 album songs) -> BREAK-KIT, a squashed 1969 funk kit as a sampler hears it.
- In chaos and storm the logistic map CHOPS THE BREAK: each sixteenth's iterate picks a piece (ghost, edit snare, open hat), the way a jungle producer slices the Amen. It is on its own track into the drums bus, so the stutter and the glass pad's cross-synthesis hear it too.
- BLIPS: the library blip (4 songs) -> c9-pulse, a new one-bit loudspeaker voice (a 6% pulse train, crushed): a machine driving its speaker directly, the oldest computer music, said sideways. It still plays the twin map on the 5:4 grid.
- MIX for the new kit (it read +7..+10 dB above 4 kHz and -12 dB at 38 Hz; cohesion 96 -> 51 at first): the master high shelf +5 -> -5 dB, lp 9k on the hats, a short E1 sine under every kick (the break kick is A#1), and the master now also lifts the 1.1 kHz hole the song always had (+3 dB) and trims 85/380 Hz. Spectrum 92.1 -> 93.7, cohesion 100.
Measured in chaos on a no-loudness copy: pulse and chop each ~8 dB under the band. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)

note:
PALETTE round. v6 96.869/96.886 (v5 rescored 96.913/96.923), kept on judgment at parity. T9_R6=steel.
- The song had no sustained, singing line: reed, blips and pulses are all staccato. Now a PEDAL STEEL (new to the album) adds one.
- As the map SETTLES (r 3.4 -> 2.9) the steel plays the period-two orbit itself: its two points as two long notes a bar, gliding one into the other. Their interval narrows bar by bar as r falls until, at r = 3 (the bifurcation point), they meet in one note: the fixed point 1 - 1/r, held to the end. The bifurcation diagram heard backwards, as a tune that closes. It is written in exact Bohlen-Pierce Hz, so nothing snaps it.
- The album-staple bell (3 songs) that marks each section becomes a HANDPAN.
Measured: steel ~7 dB and handpan ~11 dB under the band. The in-seam spectral distance to t8 is 7.98 -> 9.36 (the handpan at bar 1). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)

note:
PALETTE round. v7 96.866/96.882 (v6 rescored on f5283535 96.871/96.891), kept on judgment at parity. T9_R7=lpg.
- c9-lpg, a new patch of my own after the West Coast: a triangle and its octave through a LOW-PASS GATE (one envelope opens the filter and the amp together, then lets both fall: the struck, vocal "bongo" of the first voltage-controlled music).
- It joins the 3:4 polyrhythmic bass as its VOICE, an octave over the sub-sine body, so the bass speaks each note instead of only humming under the floor. The master 1.15 kHz lift drops 3 -> 1.5 dB, since the pluck now fills that hole.
- What did not keep (in the generator as opt-ins): replacing the bass outright with c9-lpg (T9_R7_BASS=lpg), and a dizi doubling the reed's accents an octave up (T9_R7_DIZI=1). Both broke the sections' returns (compscore recurrence 100 -> 56-85, 4 returns -> 2): a plucked, pitch-dependent timbre makes sections stop resembling each other.
Pluck ~7 dB under the band. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

- THE ORBIT AS A TUNE: a STEEL PAN (new to the album) plays the attractor's own orbit as an eighth-note ostinato: the four points of period four, round and round, growing louder.
- At the bifurcation (bar 1 of the 5/4 section) the tune DOUBLES to the eight points of period eight. That eight-note figure turns against the ten eighths of each 5/4 bar, so it lands differently every bar.
- At 256b it stops, exactly where the choir (v5) freezes the same eight points into a chord: the tune becomes the chord.
- Written in exact Bohlen-Pierce Hz. New track only. sections --against: w4 residual -7.1 dB, w5 -34 (room tail), the rest at the -45 dB mastering floor. w4 change vs w3 0.495 -> 0.630.

- IT COMES BACK: a KOTO (new to the album) knocks the map off its attractor and lets it return, one iterate per eighth.
- End of `one` (r 2.9, where the fixed point is about to lose its footing, multiplier -0.9): the knocked value spirals home slowly, high-low-high, narrowing. The period-two alternation is heard coming before it arrives.
- In `two`: every other 7/8 bar is a knock and its return in seven eighths (seven iterates). Each knock is a different size and side, so the lick recurs but never repeats.
- Under it a TABLA (new to the album) plays a 3+2+2 cycle in the 7/8, with a te-re fill every fourth bar.

PALETTE round. v10 96.784/96.816 (v9 rescored on 5cffa033 96.813/96.829), kept on judgment at parity. T9_R10=bpclar.
- The lead leaves the library clarinet (3 album songs) for c9-bpclar, this song's own BOHLEN-PIERCE CLARINET. Bohlen-Pierce is the clarinet's scale: a cylindrical bore sounds odd harmonics, and BP repeats at the 3:1 tritave, not the octave.
- The reed carries a quiet sine at exactly 3:1 (an osc layer, ratio 3): the third harmonic, the tritave, hummed on top of every note. No vibrato, a steadier pitch, a little more breath.
- In the calm sections (the period-3 window, the settle) it plays SUBTONE (^sub): breathy, dark, close.
- Tuning: pushed bright (pressure 0.52, bright 0.5, lp 4.5k) it read +2.5 dB / +200 Hz centroid and cost spectrum (s0 96.75). Without subtone it was 96.725. The darker reed (0.46/0.38/3.6k) at -2.5 dB track gain sits at parity.

note:
WHOLE-SONG round. v11 96.888/96.95 (v10 rescored on 709cf900 96.866/96.902). T9_R11=d.
- D FROM OUTSIDE. Both neighbours live on D: Kept in Mercury (t8) ends on a D-minor colour, Call and Return (t10) opens on a loud D4. This song is in Bohlen-Pierce on A, which has no D, and met neither seam (flow 59).
- So D becomes the note from outside the system: the handpan that marks every bifurcation now strikes D4 in exact Hz (unsnapped). It is a neighbour's note heard through the wall at each doubling, ringing against the tritave scale.
- The song opens on t8's own chord (A3 D4 F4 A4 D5 on the glass pad, still 12-EDO there) before the map takes it.
- At the end the floor leaves six beats early, the last chords turn D-F-G-D, a last D4 bell strikes and a choir holds D4+D5 into the tail for t10 to answer.
- Flow 59 -> 62/63 (in-seam level jump 5.2 -> 3.1 dB); spectrum 92.4 -> 91.5.
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

WHOLE-SONG round. v12 96.815/96.868 (v11 rescored on ade7b930 96.887/96.949), kept on judgment at parity (-0.07). T9_R12=henon.
- A SECOND MAP. Through the chaos section the logistic map gets company: wM's new gen: henon, the two-dimensional strange attractor (x <- 1 - a x^2 + y, y <- b x; a 1.4, b 0.3). It plays both its axes at once.
- Since y is only x one step late (times b), the two axes are a CANON the attractor writes by itself. A XYLOPHONE (new to the album) reads x on the Lambda mode of Bohlen-Pierce from A4; a MARIMBA reads y a tritave down and one step behind.
- It jumps where the logistic line folds: two chaoses, one written, one answering.
- Placements scored on s0: chaos + storm 96.70 (sections 11 -> 9, returns 4 -> 2: one timbre over both stretches joins them); storm only 96.78; chaos only 96.82, the default. T9_HEN_SECS=both|storm stay opt-in. New tracks only.

PALETTE round. v14 96.746/96.808 beats v13 (rescored on 758ba1dc 96.740/96.790). T9_R14=terrain.
- THE ORBIT GETS ITS OWN VOICE. The orbit choir (the logistic map's period eight, held as a chord) was the library's choir-classic.
- It is now WAVE TERRAIN (Bischoff, Gold and Horton, 1978; wM's new layer; new to the album): an orbit circling over a surface of hills and hollows once per period, the heights under it the wave.
- The orbit runs a hair off closing (ratio 1.003), so each held note slowly drifts through shapes, and an LFO walks its centre across the hills. No filter: the timbre moves because the orbit does. A song about orbits voiced by one. Level-matched (terrain is +4.6 dB louder).
- Also tried on s0: the closing D hold as terrain 96.715 (seam flow to t10 61.1 -> 60.6: the D it hands over wants the choir's breath); the main pad too 96.376 (spectrum 90 -> 88, flow 57: brighter, and everywhere). Both opt-in (T9_R14_DHOLD=on, T9_R14_PAD=on).
